title: Global-sections acyclicity of injective pushforwards on ringed topoi
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be sites small relative to a common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], and let $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C},\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}$ be sheaves of commutative rings. Let $f:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O_{\mathcal C})\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D),\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Its module direct image is the underlying abelian direct image with the scalar action induced by the structural ring map. For every injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module sheaf $I$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-sp-injective-resolutions] and every integer $p>0$,
$$R^p\Gamma(\mathcal D,-)(f_*I)=0.$$
Here $\Gamma(\mathcal D,M)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}(1,M_{\mathrm{sets}})$ with its induced abelian-group structure, and its right derived functors are computed by injective resolutions in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The geometric morphism need not be induced by a functor between the given sites, and no flatness of $f^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal D}\to\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 072Z, lemma-direct-image-injective-sheaf, followed by Tag 0731(3), lemma-limp-acyclic: total acyclicity implies acyclicity for module global sections.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-injective-pushforward-totally-acyclic] to $f$ and $I$, with $K=1$ the terminal sheaf of sets on $\mathcal D$. Its hypotheses are exactly those of the statement: the same sites small in the common coefficient universe, the same sheaves of commutative rings, the same morphism of ringed topoi with its induced module direct image, an injective $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$-module $I$, no flatness, and no presentation of $f$ by a functor between the given sites. Its functor $\Gamma(1,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)}(1,N_{\mathrm{sets}})$ with pointwise operations is the functor $\Gamma(\mathcal D,N)$ of the statement: the pointwise sum of $x,y:1\to N_{\mathrm{sets}}$ is the composite of $(x,y):1\to N\times N$ with the addition of $N$, which is the induced abelian-group structure. Both derived functors are computed by injective resolutions in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_{\mathcal D})$ [def-sp-left-exact-additive], so $R^p\Gamma(\mathcal D,-)(f_*I)=H^p(1,f_*I)=0$ for every $p>0$.
